externalParameters.attests: The sha256 of each subject is the EXACT, audited content of that standalone, zero-VIGIL verifier. A third party re-hashes the file they downloaded and compares it to the pinned subject digest; a mismatch means the file is not the audited one.

verifier_roles.docs/proof-carrying-finding/verify_pcf.p: PCF v0.1 reference verifier — authenticity (m-of-n Ed25519) + binding + faithful projection + the out-of-band trust-root pin, over a proof bundle / certificate.
verifier_roles.docs/proof-carrying-finding/verify_vf.py: Verifiable-Fact lifecycle verifier — prove-certificate authenticity, attestation series, witnessed time bound, AND zero-VIGIL RE-EXECUTION of the pure oracle bodies (verdict re-derivation).
verifier_roles.engine/crucible/framework/v2/evidence/au: External-audit-package re-verifier (shipped verbatim as verify_offline.py) — authenticity + binding + artifact integrity + chain/anti-suppression + the out-of-band trust-root pin.

externalParameters.zero_vigil_property: Each subject imports NO framework/vigil/crucible/strix/gateway code — it runs with the Python standard library and one Ed25519 library (cryptography). This provenance file does NOT relax that; the drift test re-confirms it by AST over the import graph.

annotations.role: PCF v0.1 wire spec the verifiers re-implement
out-of-band publication of the trust-root fingerprint + pins
durable committed transparency record of the pins

irreducible_boundary.fixture_signing_key: The default signing key is a deterministic, committed-public-seed FIXTURE key (non-governance), so CI is byte-stable with nothing provisioned. Published provenance re-signs with the operator's governance key (--signing-key; FATAL-2).
irreducible_boundary.no_hardware_root: Origin is anchored to an out-of-band-pinned Ed25519 trust root, NOT to a hardware root of trust (TEE) — see docs/limitations LIMIT-attest-tee-hardware.
irreducible_boundary.not_an_external_certification: This is certifiable-READY provenance (integrity + origin of the verifier bytes under a pinned trust root). It is NOT a Common-Criteria / FedRAMP / third-party certification; that requires an external accredited body (see docs/limitations LIMIT-external-audit-team).

builder.note: deterministic: the statement is a pure function of the verifier bytes + committed spec references; mint is idempotent and byte-reproducible.
